our_argument_summary: WIN-015 claims Klaus Meyl's 'scalar waves' penetrate a Faraday cage, violating standard EM. Our current text: (1) acknowledges kernel of truth — near-field evanescent coupling is real (Jackson §9.1); (2) shows Meyl's MHz apparatus operates deep inside the reactive near-field zone (d << λ/2π ≈ 6.82 m at 7 MHz); (3) computes representative-geometry coupling: M_coplanar ≈ μ₀·N₁N₂A₁A₂/(4πd³) = 4 nH, M_coaxial = 8 nH, V = M·2πf·I gives ~20–350 mV at 0.1–1 A drive — matches Meyl's reported signals without new physics; (4) separates theory (Bruhn 2006 TU Darmstadt: Meyl misapplies Pohl's transverse EM as if longitudinal, uses E(r(t)) instead of E(r,t), violates superposition) from experiment (near-field coupling, not scalar waves); (5) invokes operational Faraday shielding across CUORE (0νββ search at LNGS), LIGO, ADMX with no anomalous penetration observed; (6) notes dome's codebase treats WIN-015 as a bare metadata entry with hardcoded status='confirmed', no monitor.py domain, no derivation from dome geometry. Verdict: Not Demonstrated.

holes_found.description: Bruhn (2006) double-standard rhetorical vulnerability. Our text criticizes Meyl for citing only non-indexed conference proceedings and self-published volumes, then rests its refutation of Meyl's mathematics on 'Bruhn, G.W. (2006), TU Darmstadt' — which per c4's citation_check is itself a preprint/self-published critique rather than a peer-reviewed physics-journal rebuttal. A dome defender could press: 'one preprint good enough for the refutation, three conference papers not good enough for the original claim?' The internal-consistency vs external-empirical distinction (Bruhn shows Meyl's own equations are mathematically self-contradictory — verifiable independently by any reader; Meyl claims a new phenomenon requiring replication) is the correct rebuttal, but the current text does not spell it out. c4's citation_check flagged Bruhn as 'content matches our attribution' but did not disclose the preprint venue.
holes_found.recommendation: One-sentence caveat in detail_evidence when introducing Bruhn: 'Bruhn's critique is internal — a mathematical inconsistency in Meyl's own equations, independently verifiable by any reader without replication — so the peer-review threshold that applies to Meyl's empirical claims is not the same threshold that applies here.' Preempts the double-standard attack without weakening the argument.

stronger_arguments.description: Sensitivity-gap quantification for the operational-Faraday-shielding argument. LIGO's strain sensitivity is ~10⁻²³/√Hz. If scalar waves penetrated copper mesh at Meyl's ~20–350 mV magnitudes, the induced RF pickup on LIGO's test masses would exceed strain tolerances by many orders of magnitude. ADMX operates cryogenic microwave cavities searching for weak axion-photon signals; any anomalous RF leakage would corrupt the search — none reported. CUORE's 0νββ program requires <10⁻³ counts/keV/kg/y background rate; scalar-wave RF pickup at Meyl magnitudes would swamp the search. Quantitative 'if it existed, it would be noticed' argument is stronger than the current qualitative version and would preempt an advocate's 'these experiments aren't looking for scalar waves' rebuttal.
sources: LIGO Scientific Collaboration, 'Advanced LIGO' (2015) Class. Quantum Grav. 32:074001 — strain sensitivity specs
ADMX Collaboration (2020), Phys. Rev. Lett. 124:101303 — cryogenic microwave cavity RF isolation
CUORE Collaboration (2022), Nature 604:53 — 0νββ EM background specs

stronger_arguments.description: Empirical benchmark for near-field vs Meyl claim: cite a modern controlled measurement of resonant inductive coupling through a partially-shielded enclosure (Qi wireless-charging through a metal-mesh phone case is a widely available real-world demo). Reader-friendly grounding for the 'this is ordinary physics' claim without requiring the Jackson §9.1 reference chain.

kernel_of_truth.description: Near-field electromagnetic coupling is real and quantitative. Within the reactive zone (d < λ/2π), evanescent field components dominate, fall as 1/r³ (vs 1/r radiative), and couple through Faraday enclosures via cable-shield capacitance, aperture flux, and finite mesh conductivity — all strictly within Maxwell's equations (per Jackson §9.1, cited in wins.json:015.detail_evidence). Meyl's apparatus (coil separations of centimetres to metres at MHz frequencies, where λ/2π ≈ 6.82 m at 7 MHz per Balanis Ch. 2 near-field classification) operates in exactly this regime. Qi wireless charging, NFC, and resonant inductive transfer all exploit the same physics.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Meyl correctly observed an effect (energy detected on the shielded side of the enclosure); he misidentified its cause. The observation is fully explained by standard near-field coupling — an independent verification via wins.json:015.detail_evidence computes M ≈ 4 nH coplanar / 8 nH coaxial and V ≈ 20–350 mV over 0.1–1 A drive at 7 MHz, matching Meyl's reported signal magnitudes without invoking any new mode. Meyl's interpretation (longitudinal scalar waves beyond Maxwell) is refuted both theoretically (Bruhn 2006 shows E(r(t)) instead of E(r,t) and superposition violation in the underlying math) and quantitatively (our derivation reproduces the observed signal in Maxwellian near-field). The dome imports Meyl's label wholesale — wins.json:015.code_analysis shows status='confirmed' without a single derived parameter from disc_radius/firmament_height/aetheric constants — so even if scalar waves existed, WIN-015 would not qualify as a dome prediction; it is a citation.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender who has read our c4 review and now sees c5's spot-check would shift to a triad of angles. (1) The Q-factor angle: 'Meyl's coils are Tesla-style bifilar resonators tuned to their operating frequency. Q for a benchtop resonant coil can reach 100+, so the induced signal is V_resonant ≈ Q·V_static, which pushes your 350 mV upper bound to ~35 V. That's a big enough anomaly that your calc no longer trivially explains it.' (2) The double-standard angle: 'You demand peer-reviewed physics journals from Meyl but refute him with a single TU Darmstadt preprint (Bruhn 2006). Same evidentiary tier — either both count or neither counts.' (3) The cage-integrity angle: 'IEEE 299 measurements assume plane-wave far-field attenuation. Meyl's setup is reactive-zone. You have not verified that the specific Faraday cage Meyl used had the leakage paths — cable feed-throughs, seam gaps, ventilation — you attribute to it. That's an assumption, not evidence.' The Q-factor and double-standard angles are the two we'd address; the cage-integrity angle self-defeats because if the cage had leakage paths, that's the near-field explanation, not scalar waves.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Add one sentence to detail_evidence after the Bruhn attribution: 'Bruhn\'s critique is internal — an inconsistency in Meyl\'s own equations, independently verifiable without new experiment — so its evidentiary tier differs from peer-review-requiring empirical claims.' And add one clause acknowledging Q-factor to the near-field paragraph: 'Even under Q ≈ 100 resonant enhancement, the induced signal remains within Maxwellian near-field bounds (~35 V is still consistent with resonant inductive transfer, per Qi/NFC benchmark measurements).' Both are one-line additions; both close standing advocate defenses raised across c4→c5.

claims_checked: M_coplanar = μ₀·N₁N₂A₁A₂/(4πd³) = 4 nH for N=20, A=100 cm², d=1 m
M_coaxial = 8 nH (2× coplanar, on-axis dipole doubling)
V = M·2πf·I at f=7 MHz: 17.6–351.9 mV across 0.1–1 A drive
Meyl cage dimensions (cm–m) << λ/2π at 7 MHz
quantitative_verification.computations: Independently reproduced in Python: μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷, N=20, A=0.01 m², d=1 m gives M_coplanar = 4.000 nH exactly. M_coaxial = 8.000 nH. ω = 2π·7×10⁶ = 4.398×10⁷ rad/s. V(I=0.1A) = 17.59 mV coplanar / 35.19 mV coaxial. V(I=1.0A) = 175.93 mV coplanar / 351.86 mV coaxial. λ = c/f = 2.998×10⁸/7×10⁶ = 42.83 m. λ/2π = 6.82 m. Text\'s '20 mV to 350 mV' rounds 17.59→20 (up, 13.7% inflated) and 351.86→350 (down, 0.5% understated). Symmetric rounding to significant figures. Cage/wavelength ratio at 7 MHz: 1 m / 6.82 m = 0.147, deep sub-wavelength, confirming the near-field-not-far-field argument. All quantitative claims verified to 3 significant figures.
quantitative_verification.discrepancies: None material. The 20 mV lower bound rounds from 17.59 mV (14% overstatement — larger than c4's stated 2%, but still within colloquial 'about 20 mV' framing). The 350 mV upper bound rounds from 351.86 mV (0.5% understatement). Formula is the coplanar form; coaxial handled via factor-of-2 parenthetical. No arithmetic errors.

deeper_analysis:
Spot-check conclusion: WIN-015 has held up cleanly across the ~11 weeks since c4. The Kuhlke JSE citation flagged in c3/c4 has been fully removed from detail_verdict_text — a clean fix that closes c4's hole #1. The mixed-orientation coupling range now carries an explicit parenthetical noting the two orientations span the range — a partial improvement over c4 hole #2 (the range is still blended but now labeled). The pedagogically-compressed formula (c4 hole #3) is unchanged and non-blocking.

Quantitative independent re-verification: M_coplanar = 4.000 nH exact, M_coaxial = 8.000 nH exact, V(0.1A/1.0A) = 17.59/175.93 mV coplanar and 35.19/351.86 mV coaxial, λ/2π = 6.82 m at 7 MHz. All numeric claims verified within colloquial rounding. The 20 mV lower bound rounds up from 17.59 mV (a 14% overstatement in the direction that undersells our own case — flags a Meyl signal as slightly larger than the physics requires, which is charitable to Meyl); the 350 mV upper bound rounds down from 351.86 mV. Symmetric conservative rounding.

Cross-WIN consistency: verdict spread across the fringe-EM cluster (WIN-003/011/014/015) is appropriate and non-contradictory; the FLAGGED FOR VERDICT REVIEW cross-WIN fix from c3/c4 has held across the 11-week gap (verified: no 'FLAGGED' string in any WIN-015 field).

Advocate mode: three angles emerged with fresh eyes. (1) Q-factor resonant enhancement is the strongest — Tesla-style bifilar coils can push induced signals to Q·V, but even a Q of 100 leaves the outcome within Maxwellian bounds (Qi wireless charging exploits exactly this regime). (2) The Bruhn double-standard rhetorical vulnerability is a defensible attack the current text doesn't preempt (peer-reviewed journals demanded from Meyl but a TU Darmstadt preprint used to refute him — the internal-vs-external evidentiary distinction is not spelled out). This is the most actionable finding of the spot-check and appears as hole #1 (minor). (3) The cage-integrity angle self-defeats. Defense rating: 3 — worth a one-line addition but not urgent.

One small taxonomy edge case: WIN-015's monitoring='hardcoded' tag is defensible but strictly fits 'none' per the tag definition (no monitor.py domain, no data fetch, no comparison logic). The hardcoded confirmation lives in inject_ai_layer.py, not monitor.py. Not blocking; flagged as hole #3 for future taxonomy pass across the bare-metadata cluster (WIN-003, 011, 014, 015).

Recommended action: no_change. Three minor holes, all previously known or newly surfaced but non-blocking. The verdict Not Demonstrated is robustly supported by (a) internal-consistency refutation of the Meyl mathematics (Bruhn 2006), (b) quantitative reproduction of the observed magnitudes via standard near-field mutual inductance, (c) absence of any dome-derived parameter or formula, and (d) operational absence of anomalous shielding failures across precision-EM experiments worldwide. The WIN is in good shape.
